Ideas

Ideas from the book

Lines from The Autonomous Enterprise on how leaders decide where agents act, how far they are trusted and who stays accountable.

Quotes

  • Share on LinkedIn: “Autonomy is earned when value compounds faster than risk.” (opens in a new tab)
  • Share on LinkedIn: “The harness, not the model, sets the autonomy ceiling.” (opens in a new tab)
  • Share on LinkedIn: “Agents decide; deterministic rules post.” (opens in a new tab)
  • Share on LinkedIn: “Human-led, agent-operated: people set intent, own outcomes and decide where not to automate.” (opens in a new tab)
  • Share on LinkedIn: “A board that funds agents first and data second pays twice.” (opens in a new tab)
  • Share on LinkedIn: “A modest model inside a strong harness can run a narrow step at L3 safely.” (opens in a new tab)
  • Share on LinkedIn: “The model is the most flexible part and the least trusted; the safety controller is the least flexible and the most trusted.” (opens in a new tab)
  • Share on LinkedIn: “An agent optimizes its target harder and more literally than a person.” (opens in a new tab)
  • Share on LinkedIn: “An agent can act thousands of times before a monthly review.” (opens in a new tab)
  • Share on LinkedIn: “The unit that moves to an agent is a decision inside a task.” (opens in a new tab)
  • Share on LinkedIn: “The agent removes the investigation, not the person.” (opens in a new tab)
  • Share on LinkedIn: “The weakest maturity dimension caps the autonomy allowed.” (opens in a new tab)
  • Share on LinkedIn: “The person who approves an agent’s actions may not change the agent’s limits, instructions or tools.” (opens in a new tab)
